title: Emrys and the Contact
premise: Wren Sterling, a private security contractor who has spent a decade erasing their own paper trail, is hired to protect Emrys Vale, a defector carrying proof that Wren's own employer orchestrated the disappearance of Flight 447 mid-air. As rival contractors close in, Wren realizes the vanished flight carried evidence of their own erased identity—and that Emrys knows it. Torn between loyalty to the handler who saved their life and the truth Emrys offers, Wren trades their last secret to the enemy to buy Emrys's safety, then chooses truth over duty at the dawn extraction, exposing the employer and finally existing under their real name.
about_author: August Oyelaran is a former risk analyst who spent six years writing threat assessments for clients he cannot name, which taught him that the best thrillers are just paperwork with the tension left in. He writes from Lagos and Lisbon, wherever the Wi-Fi is honest.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine protection detail in Lisbon establishes Wren's craft: packed bag, three identities, no photographs. They take a new client—Emrys Vale, nervous, too well-informed about Wren's agency. The beat is controlled competence masking loneliness; Wren notices Emrys watching them like he already knows them.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vetting Emrys turns up nothing—no records before 2019, same as Wren. Handler Marguerite orders Wren to copy his files nightly, a breach of contract that stings. Emotional beat: unease. Wren obeys, telling themselves it's professionalism, not curiosity about a man who mirrors their own erasure.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On a red-eye to Geneva, Emrys watches the airline's app lose the flight mid-air—no crash report, no passengers, no tail number. He clutches an encrypted drive and understands his window is closing. The beat is cold dread: the machinery that deletes people has started running early.

chapters.title: Paper Ghost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Landing records confirm Flight 447 never existed; air traffic control tapes are 'corrupted.' Marguerite orders Wren to deliver Emrys to a 'debrief' in Zurich. Wren recognizes debrief-speak for disposal. Beat: first crack in loyalty—the lie they polished starts chafing.

chapters.title: The Zurich Debrief
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren walks Emrys into a safehouse that's clearly an ambush, then breaks protocol at the door, claiming a tail. They go dark together. Beat: betrayal of duty in real time, adrenaline and shame tangled. Emrys says, 'You're on the drive too,' and Wren doesn't ask how.

chapters.title: What the Drive Says
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a basement flat, Emrys shows fragments: the employer, Halcyon Risk Group, runs 'reconciliation' flights that erase witnesses—including a 2011 flight that deleted a teenage witness named Wren Sterling. Beat: vertigo. Wren's invisibility wasn't chosen; it was done to them, and they've been guarding the people who did it.

chapters.title: Marguerite Calls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She gives Wren twelve hours to return with Emrys or be flagged as an asset loss—which means hunted. Her tenderness toward Wren is genuine and weaponized; she pulled them out of nowhere in 2011 and built them. Beat: love against duty from the other side of the gun.

chapters.title: Two Liars, One Bed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hiding in Porto, Wren and Emrys trade biographies over cheap wine—his defection from Halcyon's data division, her fabricated pasts. Attraction sharpens into trust neither can afford. Beat: intimacy as risk. Wren admits the 2011 memory gap; Emrys admits he chose Wren specifically.

chapters.title: He Chose Me
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fury and hurt: Emrys needed a guard whose deletion Halcyon would want buried—a bodyguard with built-in motive to defect. Wren nearly walks. Beat: betrayal inside honesty. Emrys counters that everything since the safehouse door has been real, and Wren can't prove otherwise.

chapters.title: Contract Killers
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Halcyon's freelance hunters find the Porto flat through a pharmacy camera. A brutal escape through tiled alleys leaves Wren grazed and Emrys shaken by how casually Wren kills to protect him. Beat: the romance meets the job description; Emrys sees what Wren is, fully, and stays.

chapters.title: The Archive Flight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Emrys reveals Flight 447 didn't vanish—it landed at a private strip in Sardinia carrying Halcyon's physical archive, including Wren's original file. Whoever holds the archive holds every ghost Halcyon made. Beat: hope with teeth. Dawn extraction is in four days; the archive can be reached in three.

chapters.title: Old Handler, New Leash
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She traces Wren via a burner slip and offers a deal: bring the drive, and she'll restore Wren's identity personally—she kept the original file out of sentiment. Beat: temptation dressed as motherhood. Marguerite believes she's saving Wren from a con man; she may even be right.

chapters.title: Sardinia
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Off-season coastal town, the hangar, the archive crates. Wren finds their own juvenile intake photo—name, birthplace, a mother's name they'd forgotten. Beat: grief surfacing as rage. Emrys watches Wren hold their stolen self and understands what he's asking them to burn down.

chapters.title: Copy or Burn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hunters hit the hangar early. In the firefight, Emrys wants the whole archive leaked; Wren wants only their file back. They compromise: copy everything, torch the rest. Beat: partnership forged under fire—two loyalties negotiating instead of one surrendering.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Price
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She intercepts them at the marina, alone, off-book. She offers Wren the restored life one final time and reveals Emrys's drive also contains the names of assets Halcyon will kill if exposed—people Marguerite trained, some Wren loved. Beat: the truth has casualties; leaking isn't clean.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reading the asset list, Wren finds two names from their old team. Emrys argues exposure saves hundreds of future targets; Wren counts the eleven on the list. Beat: moral deadlock between lovers. Wren pockets the list without telling Emrys what they intend to do with it.

chapters.title: What I Traded
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To buy Emrys a clear runway, Wren contacts Halcyon directly and offers the one secret worth killing for: where Emrys will be at dawn—in exchange for the eleven names being scrubbed from all lists. Beat: self-erasure again, this time chosen, as sacrifice disguised as treachery.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The extraction plane waits on a fog-bound strip. Halcyon's teams converge on the coordinates Wren sold—but Wren sold a false site and kept the real runway, betting Marguerite would rather defect than watch Wren die. Beat: climax. Gunfire in fog, Marguerite's choice, Emrys learning Wren's 'betrayal' was armor.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Last Filing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Shot covering Wren's flank, she uploads Halcyon's internal ledger to three journalists before the hunters reach her, whispering that she kept Wren's file because someone should have come for her once. Beat: tragic grace—duty and love reconciled too late, truth delivered by the loyalist.

chapters.title: Airborne
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The extraction plane lifts at dawn with Emrys, the copied archive, and the ledger going public beneath them. Wren confesses the trade and the false coordinates; Emrys confesses he'd have traded Wren's secret too, weeks ago, before the safehouse door. Beat: exhausted honesty—love surviving full disclosure.

chapters.title: Real Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, testifying from shadow to an inquiry, Wren uses their birth name aloud for the first time since 2011. The go-bag sits unpacked by the door. Beat: quiet resolution—identity reclaimed not as a document but as a decision, spoken in a room full of strangers.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Contact
chapters.summary: Dual POV coda. Emrys publishes under his own name; Wren takes a legitimate security consulting license with their real one. On a Lisbon rooftop they argue about whether to keep a go-bag 'for tradition.' Beat: earned peace with vigilance—two people who were deleted, now permanently on the record, together.
